title: For a glueing pair the first Tor of the bigger ring with the cokernel of localizing a module at the element vanishes
author: The Stacks Project Authors
work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra)
source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
difficulty_reason: The lemma takes a glueing pair (R -> R', f) and asserts that for every R-module M one has Tor^R_1(R', Coker(M -> M_f)) = 0 (source lines 25498-25505). The proof proceeds in three stages. It first sets M-bar = M/M[f^infty], notes that Coker(M -> M_f) is isomorphic to Coker(M-bar -> M-bar_f), and therefore assumes f is a nonzerodivisor on M; in that case M is contained in M_f, M_f/M is the colimit of M/f^nM with multiplication transitions, and since Tor commutes with colimits it suffices to prove Tor^R_1(R', M/f^nM) = 0 (proof lines 25508-25515). The special case M = R/R[f^infty] is then done by an explicit diagram: the same-f-torsion lemma gives M tensor_R R' = R'/R'[f^infty], and from the short exact sequence 0 -> M -> M -> M/f^nM -> 0 the long exact Tor sequence produces the displayed commutative diagram in which the diagonal arrow is injective; since Tor_1^R(R', R/R[f^infty]) vanishes by the first-Tor-total lemma, the proof deduces Tor_1^R(R', M/f^nM) = 0 (proof lines 25518-25537). The general case reduces to this one: the proof chooses a surjection F -> M with F a free R/R[f^infty]-module and forms 0 -> N -> F/f^nF -> M/f^nM -> 0, which by the torsion-completion lemma stays exact after tensoring with R'; since Tor_1^R(R', F/f^nF) vanishes by the previous paragraph, so does Tor_1^R(R', M/f^nM) (proof lines 25540-25550). The non-routine content is the diagram in the special case and the reduction that removes the f-torsion from M.
